Verify that no int6/uint4/uint2 memory-op nodes remain in the lowered IR.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that emits vectorized cast sequences from low-precision types to float16/bfloat16 using CUDA PRMT, LOP3, and bitwise instructions, keeping all operations within registers without inter-thread communication.

verification.spec: Compile a Tilus program that casts a register tensor of type uint4/int4/float6 to float16. Inspect the generated PTX for 'prmt.b32', 'lop3.b32', and bitwise 'shl/shr/and/or' ops. Assert that no shared-memory stores/loads and no shfl.sync instructions appear inside the cast sequence (i.e., cast is entirely register-local, per-thread).

sub_tasks.requirements: After lowering, memory-loading operations for low-precision tensors are replaced by loads of standard uint8 types (thanks to the reinterpretation), so no per-element bitwise unpacking is performed inside the main loop.

verification.spec: Compile a low-precision matmul kernel (e.g., f16 x uint4) with Tilus. Inspect the innermost K-loop body in the emitted CUDA/PTX and assert that all weight loads are typed uint8 (u8) vector loads and there are no per-element bitwise unpacking sequences (and/shr masks over sub-byte fields) inside the loop between memory load and the vectorized cast. The unpacking must appear only in the vectorized cast step, not the load path.

sub_tasks.requirements: Step 4 of compilation and execution: the runtime system dynamically loads compiled binaries, provides an execution context, and maintains a kernel cache.
Code has been implemented for a runtime that dynamically loads compiled hardware binaries (via the CUDA driver API or equivalent) and exposes them as callable kernel handles.

verification.spec: Compile a trivial Tilus kernel (e.g., copy or add). From Python, invoke the runtime's kernel loader to load the compiled cubin/binary and launch it on a small tensor via the returned callable handle. Assert that the kernel executes and produces correct output, exercising the dynamic-load path (cuModuleLoad / cuLaunchKernel or equivalent).

sub_tasks.requirements: The runtime allocates an on-demand global workspace that compiled kernels can request via the AllocateGlobal instruction, and grows or reuses this workspace across kernel launches.

verification.spec: Write a Tilus kernel that issues AllocateGlobal for a workspace of size S. Launch it twice with increasing S; between launches, query the runtime's workspace size and confirm it grew (or was reused if S is smaller). Verify the workspace pointer is valid inside the kernel by writing and reading back a marker value.

sub_tasks.requirements: The runtime maintains an execution context storing the CUDA stream on which kernels are launched and forwards the stream to each kernel invocation.

verification.spec: Create two CUDA streams via torch.cuda.Stream. Launch the same Tilus kernel on each stream through the runtime's execution context. Verify (via cudaStreamQuery or event-based recording) that the kernel launched on stream A synchronized only with events on stream A. Assert the runtime's context object exposes/accepts a stream parameter that is forwarded to the underlying cuLaunchKernel call.

sub_tasks.requirements: The runtime maintains an in-memory cache of compiled kernels keyed by program identity and tuning parameters, so that repeated launches of the same kernel avoid recompilation.

verification.spec: Compile a Tilus program once (with timing), then call the same compiled program a second time with identical parameters and time again. Assert the second call's compile/lookup time is at least 100x smaller than the first (indicating cache hit). Also verify a different parameter set triggers a fresh compile.

sub_tasks.requirements: Compiling all approximately 200 auto-tuning configurations for a single low-precision matmul operator completes in roughly one minute on the reference machine.

verification.spec: Trigger a full auto-tuning compilation of the low-precision matmul template (e.g., uint4 weight) with all ~200 configurations. Wall-clock the total compilation phase (excluding first-time nvcc warmup for the standard library). Report elapsed seconds.

depends_on: Thread-Block-Level Programming Model and Instruction Set

sub_tasks.requirements: A single parameterized Tilus program template for low-precision matmul (as shown in Figure 2) is implemented, supporting all evaluated quantized data types via tunable tile-size hyperparameters, with the auto-tuning mechanism (~200 configurations, ~1 minute compile time).
The Tilus program template for low-precision matmul C = A x B is implemented following the structure of Figure 2, with parameterizable tile sizes (BM, BN, BK) and configurable data types for A and B.
Code has been implemented that defines a Tilus program (matmul kernel) with a grid shape of (M / BM, N / BN), where BM and BN are tunable tile-size hyperparameters exposed as template parameters.

verification.spec: Import the Tilus matmul program source and instantiate it with parameters (BM, BN). Query the program's grid shape and assert it evaluates to (M/BM, N/BN) symbolically or for a chosen concrete (M, N). Confirm BM and BN are exposed as tunable/template parameters (e.g., appear in the program's tunable spec).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that uses the BlockIndices instruction to retrieve thread-block indices (bi, bj) inside the kernel and computes the (bi*BM, bj*BN) offset into the output C tile.

verification.spec: Dump the Tilus IR of the matmul kernel and grep for a BlockIndices instruction whose outputs (bi, bj) are used as multiplicative offsets by BM and BN into the global tensor view of C. Assert both (bi*BM) and (bj*BN) expressions are present in the IR.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that creates global-memory tensor views for the A, B, and C operands with explicit shape and address specification via the GlobalView (or equivalent) instruction.

verification.spec: Inspect the matmul program IR and assert that three GlobalView (or equivalent) instructions are created, one for each of A, B, and C, each carrying an explicit shape and pointer/address argument matching the kernel parameters.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that allocates the C accumulator as a register tensor whose layout is the Kronecker composition local(2,1).spatial(8,4).local(1,2), matching the mma.m16n8k16 tensor-core output layout.

verification.spec: Locate the C accumulator allocation in the matmul IR. Assert its layout is the Kronecker composition local(2,1) x spatial(8,4) x local(1,2) (checkable via layout.spatial_modes and local_modes attributes or a to-string equal to 'local(2,1).spatial(8,4).local(1,2)'). Verify shape is (16, 8).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that emits a range-based reduction loop over the K dimension with step BK, loading tiles of A and B and accumulating their product into the C register tensor each iteration.

verification.spec: Inspect the matmul IR and confirm the presence of a range-based for loop over k with step BK. Inside the loop body, assert LoadGlobal instructions for A and B tiles and a Dot (mma) instruction whose output writes/accumulates into the C register tensor.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that stores the C accumulator back to global memory at the end of the kernel, including any final cast (e.g., f32 to f16) from the accumulator type to the output type.

verification.spec: Compile and run the matmul kernel with a small (M,N,K), then read back the C output tensor. Assert (a) the output dtype is f16, (b) the kernel emits a Cast(f32->f16) followed by StoreGlobal at the end of the program (verified via IR inspection), and (c) the computed values match a torch.matmul reference within f16 tolerance (rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2).

sub_tasks.requirements: The low-precision weight-loading pipeline of Figure 2 (b/c) is implemented inside the template, covering the pre-launch layout rearrangement, register load, reinterpretation, and vectorized cast steps.

Code has been implemented that, as an offline pre-processing step before kernel launch, rearranges the low-precision weight tensor B from shape [K, N] to a tiled uint8 storage layout u8[K/BK, N/BN, BK*BN*bits/8] following the procedure of Figure 9.

verification.spec: Given a reference int6 weight tensor B of shape [K=128, N=256], run the preprocessing routine to obtain a uint8 buffer of shape [K/BK, N/BN, BK*BN*6/8]. Independently decode the u8 buffer back to int6 values using the documented bit-packing scheme and assert element-wise equality with the original B (after applying the same tile permutation).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that loads the rearranged uint8 weight tile from global memory into a register tensor with layout local(n2).spatial(T).local(n1) using the LoadGlobal instruction, enabling coalesced vectorized transactions.

verification.spec: In the matmul IR after preprocessing, locate the LoadGlobal that loads the packed weight into registers. Assert the target register tensor's dtype is uint8 and its layout matches local(n2).spatial(T).local(n1) with n1 = gcd(n,16) and n2 = n/gcd(n1,16), for the tile's per-thread byte count n and thread count T. Verify emitted PTX uses vectorized ld.global.v4.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that reinterprets the loaded uint8 register tensor as a low-precision-dtype register tensor with a tensor-core-compatible layout at zero cost, verifying that both tensors occupy the same bit count per thread.

verification.spec: Construct a uint8 register tensor with 3 elements per thread across 32 threads (24 bits/thread). Invoke the reinterpret operation to view it as int6 with 4 elements per thread and a tensor-core-compatible layout. Assert (a) the reinterpret succeeds only when bits_per_thread match (test a failure case with 20 bits), and (b) the emitted code contains no memory ops or shuffles for the reinterpret (pure type/layout metadata change).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that performs a vectorized cast from the reinterpreted low-precision register tensor to the compute dtype (e.g., float16), using PRMT/LOP3/bitwise PTX instructions where applicable.

verification.spec: Create a small Tilus program that casts a register tensor of dtype int6 (packed in u8) to f16 using the vectorized cast. Run it on known input values and compare against a numpy reference (int6 -> float16). Additionally inspect emitted PTX and assert prmt.b32 and lop3.b32 instructions are present.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that loads the high-precision A tile (e.g., f16[16,16]) from global memory into registers with a layout matching the mma tensor-core A-operand requirement.

verification.spec: In the matmul IR, locate the LoadGlobal that populates the A register tile. Assert dtype is f16, shape is (16, 16), and the layout matches the mma.m16n8k16 A-operand requirement (e.g., local(1,2).spatial(8,4).local(1,2) or its documented equivalent). Verify tile offset uses (bi*BM, k).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that issues an mma (matrix-multiply-accumulate) tensor-core instruction on the loaded A tile and the cast B tile, accumulating into the C register tensor each K-iteration.

verification.spec: Inspect the matmul IR loop body: assert one Dot instruction per k-iteration with operands (A_reg, B_cast_reg) writing into the C accumulator (in-place). Confirm compilation emits mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16 in the generated PTX.

sub_tasks.requirements: The template supports all evaluated quantized weight data types (uint1-uint8, int2-int8, float3-float8 with arbitrary exponent/mantissa) and multiple activation dtypes through the same parameterized program.

Code has been implemented that parameterizes the weight dtype of the template such that a single program source can be instantiated with any of uint1..uint8, int2..int8, and float3..float8 (with configurable exponent/mantissa) without code duplication.

verification.spec: Instantiate the same matmul program template with weight dtypes uint1, uint4, uint8, int2, int4, int8, float3(e2m0), float4(e2m1), float6(e3m2), and float8(e4m3). For each, successfully compile the program without source modification (only parameter change) and run a small correctness check against a dequantized reference. Assert all instantiations succeed.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports float16, bfloat16, and int8 as the activation (A operand) dtype in the same template, selecting appropriate accumulator and mma instructions per activation type.

verification.spec: Instantiate the Tilus matmul template three times with A operand dtype in {float16, bfloat16, int8} and a low-precision weight (e.g., uint4). For each activation dtype, verify the kernel compiles, selects an appropriate accumulator (fp32 for f16/bf16, i32 for int8) and mma instruction, runs successfully on an H100, and produces outputs within tolerance of a reference numpy/torch matmul with dequantized weights.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, given a weight tensor with n bytes per thread and T threads, automatically derives the uint8 reinterpret layout local(n2).spatial(T).local(n1) with n1 = gcd(n,16) and n2 = n/gcd(n1,16) as specified in Section 7.2.

verification.spec: Call the layout-derivation function with representative (n_bytes_per_thread, T) pairs such as (3, 32), (6, 32), (12, 32), (16, 32), (24, 32). Assert the returned layout is uint8 local(n2).spatial(T).local(n1) where n1=gcd(n,16) and n2=n/gcd(n1,16). Cross-check numerically against the paper's formula in Section 7.2.

sub_tasks.requirements: The auto-tuning mechanism for the low-precision matmul template is implemented, exploring the tile-size configuration space and caching compiled kernels.

verification.spec: For each of {A100, L40S, H100}: run QWen2.5-30B decode with 16 tokens using Tilus uint4 and Ladder uint4 kernels integrated via vLLM; median over 10 runs; on H100, Ladder is expected to ERR (kernel invalid) and Tilus must succeed; on A100 and L40S, assert latency_ladder / latency_tilus >= 1.2 (i.e., Tilus at least 1.2x faster). Report the A100 speedup and check against paper: 244/146 ~= 1.67x with tolerance 0.30.

sub_tasks.paper_unit: x speedup (Ladder/Tilus on A100 decode BS=16)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that Tilus uint4 matmul speedup over cuBLAS f16 grows with decreasing batch size in the decode regime, exhibiting >=2x speedup at BS=1 and monotonically non-increasing speedup as BS grows to 16 for K=N in {4096,8192,12288}

verification.spec: Run cuBLAS f16 and Tilus uint4 matmul for BS in {1,4,8,16} and (K=N) in {4096,8192,12288}; compute speedup = latency_cublas / latency_tilus for each; assert speedup at BS=1 is >= 2.0 for K=N=8192 (tolerance 0.30 around paper value ~2.8) and speedup at BS=16 is lower than at BS=1 for the same shape

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that Tilus generates working matmul kernels for the full spectrum of weight data types (uint1-8, int2-8, float3-8 with common exp/mantissa splits) at BS=16, K=8192, N=57344, and speedup vs cuBLAS f16 monotonically increases as bit width decreases within each type kind

verification.spec: For weight dtypes in {uint1..uint8, int2..int8, float3..float8 (e4m3,e3m3,e3m2,e2m2,e2m1,e1m1)}, compile and run Tilus matmul at (BS=16, K=8192, N=57344); assert all kernels succeed; compute speedup vs cuBLAS f16; assert uint1 speedup >= 6.0 (paper 9.4x, tolerance 0.35) and that within uint kind, speedup(uint1) > speedup(uint4) > speedup(uint8)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that disabling software pipelining (removing pipelined cp.async in the Tilus weight-loading loop) increases decode-stage matmul latency by a measurable amount for BS=16 uint4 kernels

verification.spec: Implement a Tilus uint4 matmul variant with software pipelining depth=1 (no overlap) and the default pipelined version; run at (BS=16, K=8192, N=8192); measure median latency; assert latency_no_pipeline / latency_pipelined >= 1.15 (paper motivates pipelining as major contributor)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that a Triton-style low-precision matmul that performs shared-memory layout conversion (Step 4 in Figure 1a) is measurably slower than the Tilus register-reinterpretation path for uint4 at BS=1

verification.spec: Compare Triton auto-tuned uint4 matmul kernel vs Tilus uint4 matmul at (BS=1, K=8192, N=8192); measure median latency over 50 runs; assert latency_triton / latency_tilus >= 1.5 (paper reports 1.75x average over Triton)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that Tilus tile-level reinterpretation supports non-power-of-two bit widths (uint6/int6/float6) efficiently while Ladder's type-level packing either fails to generate a kernel or is significantly slower for the same shape

verification.spec: Attempt to build/run Ladder (bitblas v0.0.1.dev15) matmul for weight dtype float6_e3m2 (or uint6) at (BS=16, K=8192, N=57344); attempt same with Tilus; if Ladder supports it, assert latency_ladder / latency_tilus >= 2.0 (paper reports 2.61x average). If Ladder cannot compile a kernel for float6, assert Tilus successfully runs and produces a valid speedup >= 3.0x vs cuBLAS f16.

Verify (a) __syncthreads() (bar.sync) is emitted, and (b) the loaded values equal the written values across 1000 launches with different inputs (no race conditions). Additionally verify that omitting Synchronize produces incorrect / non-deterministic outputs.
